items.title: Disjoint Borel annuli that every injective ray meets infinitely often at Borel asymptotic separation index one
items.author: Felix Weilacher
items.work: Borel Edge Colorings for Finite Dimensional Groups
items.difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the article's Lemma lem:rainbow at source lines 173-175: from asi_B(G)=1 and a dimension d it must produce pairwise disjoint Borel sets V_i that every injective G-ray meets infinitely often. The construction can only be read off after fixing the two-piece Borel partition at the scale N=4d+1 and taking V_i = A(U_0,2(i-1),2i) (source line 180), and the real work is then to rule out the one way it could fail, namely a ray that keeps within distance 2d of U_0; that step needs the finite-component hypothesis on G^{<=N} restricted to U_0 together with local finiteness (source line 182) and a separate symmetric argument for U_0. Local combinatorics of a single ray does not give this, because the hypothesis is a global finiteness condition on distance-N components and the annuli exist only relative to a partition chosen beforehand; the change-of-distance-by-one step at line 184 is what finally converts a crossing of the two pieces into an edge inside every annulus.
